# Permission is a named profile, not a mode

> A deny rule survives the most permissive base mode while an allow rule is inert under it, so the permissive mode you actually run can stay and still gate what is irreversible.

Applies to `crates/bancada-core/**`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **Permission mode per runtime** (nothing refuses it) — Leaves the real gap: inside one runtime, irreversible infrastructure work and ordinary code get identical treatment.
- **Mode chosen at session start** (nothing refuses it) — Requires predicting what the session will touch. A tool-class policy catches it when it happens.

## What keeps it

Nothing can. It describes the shape of a configuration the product reads, not the shape of the code that reads it.
